reviewHistory: One round on the exact merged head 38e05413 by an independent Fable 5.1 reviewer (run through cliproxy): APPROVE-WITH-NOTES with no blockers and no majors, three documentary minors M1-M3 and notes N1-N7; none requires a change to the head.
verdictText: Verdict: APPROVE-WITH-NOTES. Blockers: none. Majors: none. Minors: M1-M3 (documentary, none requires a change to this PR). Notes N1-N7. Carry-forwards for TS7S2B/S3/S4B/S5A/S2OD: section 7.

behaviourEquality.statement: The three stdout hashes match the author's red/local receipts (8bf31f80..., 2d000d64..., da8a0fc5...). stderr: base prints the 4-line Node MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning (its pid and path vary, so its hash varies per run; it vanished when the tool called process.exit(1) synchronously); head prints nothing. No tool output goes to stderr on either side.
behaviourEquality.note: The reviewer re-ran the four terminology commands plus validate report, --json and --help on base 35b962d7 (ts-node) and head 38e05413 (tsx) with stdout and stderr captured as raw bytes, and a deliberate-violation probe on both trees: stdout and exit codes are identical apart from the six intended --help lines (section 2).

typeCheckOnLoad.wording: Type-checking on load. ts-node type-checks by default and did so here: a copy of the tool with one appended `const x: number = 'x'` fails under npx ts-node with TSError TS2322 even for --help (exit 1, no stdout); the same file under tsx on both trees runs (exit 0, help printed). No TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY, tsconfig "ts-node" key, or --transpile-only flag is in the tree, so the old npm scripts were type-checking the tool on every run and the new ones do not. This is covered elsewhere: `tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck --listFilesOnly` on the head lists openspec/scripts/terminology-tool.ts, terminology-tool.types.ts, spec-purpose-lint.ts and (allowJs) terminology-tool.core.js/.fixers.js/.output.js, because the root tsconfig includes **/*.ts and excludes only scripts/** and desktop/**. npm run typecheck exits 0 on the head. So the tool stays type-checked by the gate that CI and the pre-commit hook run; nothing is lost. (N1)

moduleSyntaxDetection.wording: What ts-node was actually doing on the base is worth recording, because it shows the swap removes fragility rather than adding it. With the root tsconfig (module esnext, moduleResolution bundler, target es2017) ts-node 10.9.2 emits ESM: `require('ts-node').create().compile(...)` on terminology-tool.ts yields `import * as fs from 'fs'; ...` (236 lines). ts-node then hands that to the CommonJS loader, and the run only succeeds because Node 22.22 detects module syntax, re-parses the file as ESM (hence the MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning) and loads a .ts URL through its type-stripping format table. Evidence: on the base, `npx ts-node ... validate` with NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-detect-module fails with "SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module" (exit 1), and with NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-strip-types fails with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION ".ts" (exit 1). On the head, `npx tsx ... validate` passes under both flags with the identical stdout 8bf31f80... (exit 0). The package engines field is node >=22.12.0; type stripping was unflagged only in 22.18, so the base command was likely broken on 22.12-22.17 (I could not test those versions: nvm has 20.20.0, 22.22.0, 24.13.0, 24.15.0 only). The head does not depend on either Node feature. (N2)

findings.summary: Two findings from section 2. (1) ts-node type-checked the tool on every load and tsx does not; the root tsc --noEmit gate covers it because the root tsconfig includes openspec/scripts/*.ts and the allowJs .js modules. (2) The base ts-node run worked only through Node module-syntax detection, require(esm) and type stripping; tsx does not depend on either feature.

lockfile.reproduced: The head package-lock.json (blob 0bc4b876) is reproduced byte for byte from the base by `node <nvm v24.15.0>/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js uninstall ts-node --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` (npm 11.19.1 under Node 22.22.0) in a clean worktree with no node_modules; the resulting package.json is also byte-identical to the head's (blob ce821c60). git diff --numstat: 9/154 as stated.
lockfile.idempotent: Idempotent: `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` with npm 11.19.1 on the head prints "up to date" and leaves 0 lines changed. With npm 11.6.2 (the npm bundled with Node 22.22.0) the same command rewrites the head lockfile by +80/-196 and the base lockfile by +90/-205 (libc/peer/dev flag churn): the churn the author discarded is a property of npm 11.6.2 against this lockfile at either commit, not of this change. (N3)
lockfile.authorConcern: Lockfile npm version: verified above; 11.19.1 reproduces and is idempotent, 11.6.2 churns both commits equally. Recording the generating npm version in the receipt, as the author did, is the right practice and should continue for TS7S3/TS7S4B (section 7).

reviewReruns: On 38e05413 and base 35b962d7 under Node v22.22.0, in throwaway worktrees (base node_modules junctioned to the root checkout with ts-node 10.9.2 and tsx 4.22.4; head node_modules junctioned to the author npm ci tree with no ts-node), the reviewer used its own capture harness. It ran the four terminology commands and validate report/--json/--help on both trees, a deliberate-violation probe on both trees, an argv runner-identity probe, a type-error injection (TS2322) under ts-node and tsx, --no-experimental-detect-module and --no-experimental-strip-types sensitivity runs, an @/ alias probe under tsx with both tsconfigs, a lockfile reproduction from base with npm 11.19.1, idempotence checks with npm 11.19.1 and 11.6.2, a JSON-level lockfile diff, npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts with both npm versions, a ts-node reference scan, and the gates npm run typecheck, lint, lint:units, format:check, openspec strict, qc:openspec-ci, desktop type-check and desktop npm test (warm and --no-cache, 57/57), the validator, --next and the validator tests (86/86). It did not re-run npm run test:stable, a full real npm ci, build, storybook:build or next dev (section 9).
notVerified: npm run test:stable (not re-run; author's single run 2796/2796 suites, 37180 passed).
A full real `npm ci` from the head lockfile into an empty directory (only --dry-run with two npm versions plus the author's existing physical tree, validated by npm ls).
Behaviour of the base command on Node 22.12-22.17 (versions not installed); the head does not depend on the features in question.

openNotesResolution.TS7S2A-OPEN-1: The three stdout hashes match the author's red/local receipts (8bf31f80..., 2d000d64..., da8a0fc5...). stderr: base prints the 4-line Node MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning (its pid and path vary, so its hash varies per run; it vanished when the tool called process.exit(1) synchronously); head prints nothing. No tool output goes to stderr on either side.
openNotesResolution.TS7S2A-OPEN-2: tsconfig handling by tsx: tsx loads the tsconfig from the cwd (register-*.mjs: loadTsconfig(process.env.TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH); npm run sets cwd to the repository root) and uses it for paths, jsx, useDefineForClassFields and the like; its esbuild target is `node${process.versions.node}` (index-*.mjs), not the tsconfig target, so target es2017 does not downlevel anything at run time. A probe file importing `{ UI_THEMES } from '@/constants/appearance'` resolves under tsx with the root tsconfig (paths without baseUrl) and, with TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=scripts/tsconfig.json, with the baseUrl form too; the same probe under ts-node on the base fails ("Cannot find package '@/constants'"), so tsx is strictly more capable here. The terminology tool itself imports only node builtins and relative files (./terminology-tool.{core,fixers,output}.js and a type-only import of ./terminology-tool.types), so no alias is exercised by the four commands.
openNotesResolution.TS7S2A-OPEN-3: Desktop TS151002 count: confirmed cache-dependent (my 14 warm / 16 cold against the author's 0 / 13 / 16); ts-jest emits them per transformed file not served from cache. No diagnostics.ignoreCodes added; desktop untouched (hashes unchanged). The 0 assertion belongs to the 2.3 receipt (C3 carried).
openNotesResolution.TS7S2A-OPEN-4: No import/require line is added anywhere.

TS7S2OD.wording: tsx resolves the `@/*` alias correctly from both the root tsconfig (paths without baseUrl) and scripts/tsconfig.json (baseUrl ../src form) when pointed at it with TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH; the terminology tool needs neither. Deleting or narrowing scripts/tsconfig.json therefore cannot change any tsx-run script's module resolution, which confirms C2 from the tsx side.

minors.wording: M1. openspec/scripts/README.md still documents npx ts-node (17 lines). Registered to TS7S5A; stale but not broken.

M2. The tool is no longer type-checked at run time (ts-node did; tsx does not). Covered by root `npm run typecheck`, which includes openspec/scripts/*.ts and the allowJs .js modules (verified with --listFilesOnly). Worth one sentence in the TS7S5A docs so nobody reads a green terminology run as a type-check.

M3. The receipts record the MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning but not why it appeared (ts-node emitting ESM under module esnext and Node rescuing it). Section 2 above records it; nothing to change.

notes.wording: N1. Type-check-on-load difference verified by injection (TS2322): ts-node exit 1 even for --help; tsx exit 0.

N2. Base ts-node run depended on Node's module-syntax detection, require(esm) and type-stripping format table; fails under --no-experimental-detect-module and --no-experimental-strip-types. Head tsx passes under both. Engines node >=22.12.0 makes the base command suspect on 22.12-22.17 (not tested).
N3. npm 11.6.2 lockfile churn is pre-existing at the base, not introduced here.
N4. Shebang form unchanged in property, non-executable file, repository convention.
N5. `validate --json` embeds absolute paths; byte-identical modulo the checkout directory name.
N6. @emnapi/runtime and @img/sharp-wasm32 show as extraneous in both the root and the author's trees; unrelated.

N7. The author's `npm ci --dry-run` without --ignore-scripts failed only because husky's prepare runs before node_modules exists; the --ignore-scripts form passes under both npm versions, as I reproduced.
